A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SEE2REFINE. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and matchable, including the new reproducibility appendices in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations, ablations, and an 18-participant human study, with detailed results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original VLM experiments, ablations, and human-study results in the main text and Appendix A.

M1.justification: The scenario-generation, rendering, kernel scoring, format-aware fine-tuning, and iterative preference-learning procedures remain unchanged. The new prompts and implementation disclosures do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same generated traffic scenarios, three eHMI modalities, and two emitter types. The human study retains the same eight scenario-message pairs and eyes/lightbar modalities.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same model, apprentice, initial-database, and ablation comparisons. The human study retains the same base-model comparison and GPT-5, Claude Opus 4.1, and Grok 4 comparators.

E3.justification: The stated splits, model sizes, training epochs, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. However, new Table 3 lists DPO beta as 0.2 and SFT mixing weight as 0.01, while Section 4.1 still states a preference coefficient of 0.01. This unresolved discrepancy prevents determining whether a setting was revised or inaccurately clarified.

E4.justification: The importance-sampling and diverse-beam ablations, across-round performance and formatting-error analysis, and Figure 7 metric-distribution analysis are retained. Added explanations of trust do not introduce new robustness experiments.

E5.justification: The uncertainty reporting and statistical procedures are unchanged, including human-rating error bars, standard deviations, repeated-measures ANOVA, effect sizes, and Appendix A reliability analyses. No new repeated-run or seed reporting appears.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain all numerical values, and Figures 4 and 7 retain their plotted results. Human-study findings remain fourth-place performance and average improvements of 7.7% for eyes and 7.9% for lightbar over the reported base model.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 retain the same kernel score, importance score, and preference-pair definitions. The new qualification that kernel weighting is a simple default adds interpretation, not a mathematical definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows VLM–human alignment from well aligned to reasonably aligned in controlled settings. The introduction explicitly positions the work as an early-stage simulation study and qualifies the contribution scope, while retaining the central refinement and human-transfer claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2.3 adds hypotheses explaining weak trust improvements through higher-level subjective judgment and omitted environmental cues, and limits applicability accordingly. v2 also qualifies kernel weighting and clarifies that rendering/evaluation costs occur during offline refinement.

D1.justification: New Appendices B–C substantially expand reproducibility documentation with evaluator prompts, the similarity-judge template, frame limits, LoRA and optimizer settings, batch size, sequence length, and NF4 inference quantization. The resource footnote replaces the anonymous repository link with a named GitHub link and no longer explicitly lists rendered clips.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and substantive relationship to predefined eHMI designs, prompt-based designers, VLM judging, and RLAIF remain unchanged. Citation cleanup and bibliographic edits do not introduce new research positioning relative to prior work.

P1.justification: v2 makes local language corrections throughout, rewrites contribution bullets, extends the conclusion, updates author information, and adds acknowledgments and documentation appendices. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3 and boxed prompt templates, refreshes existing diagrams, corrects boldface emphasis in Table 1, relocates Figure 4, and adjusts captions and page layout. The existing result plots preserve their content.

improvement.justification: The added evaluator prompts and training documentation make the work more reproducible, while qualifications in the abstract and introduction better match the controlled evidence. These benefits outweigh the limited drawbacks, but the unresolved DPO-coefficient discrepancy between Section 4.1 and Table 3 prevents a fully consistent training specification.
